gap: The paper names CrisisBench v1.0 English humanitarian files but gives no download URL, exact file names, checksum, or label-mapping table.

Reconstruct from the eight original source datasets
chosen: Use the official CrisisBench v1.0 English humanitarian consolidated release with its predefined Train, Development and Test splits.
rationale: The paper cites CrisisBench [4] and reports the expected 87,455 records across predefined splits.
quote: This study utilises the CrisisBench v1.0 English humanitarian classification dataset.

gap: Label ordering and whether Macro-F1 averages over all 11 labels or only labels present in each split are not specified.
options: Average over all 11 fixed CrisisBench labels
Average only over labels present in y_true and y_pred
chosen: Use all 11 CrisisBench labels in a fixed order and compute Macro-F1 over all 11 labels.
rationale: The paper states that all labels were retained and that each of the 11 labels contributed equally.
quote: All 11 labels were retained without merging.

gap: LinearSVC loss, penalty, dual setting, tolerance and maximum iterations beyond C and class_weight are not stated.

chosen: Use scikit-learn LinearSVC defaults for unspecified hyperparameters, including squared_hinge loss, L2 penalty and default multiclass one-vs-rest behaviour.
rationale: The paper names LinearSVC and scikit-learn but reports only C and class_weight, so library defaults are the conventional choice.
quote: LinearSVC with word unigram–bigram TF-IDF, C=0.5 and balanced class weighting.

gap: The exact token pattern and tokenizer are not specified beyond saying no separate custom tokenisation was applied.
options: Use scikit-learn TfidfVectorizer default token_pattern and preprocessor
chosen: Use scikit-learn TfidfVectorizer default token_pattern and preprocessor.
rationale: The paper explicitly says no separate custom tokenisation step was applied and uses scikit-learn.
quote: No stop-word filtering, stemming, lemmatisation or separate custom tokenisation step was applied.

gap: Whether TfidfVectorizer should lowercase again after the manual lowercase preprocessing step is unspecified.
options: Manual lowercase plus TfidfVectorizer default lowercase=True
chosen: Apply manual lowercase in preprocessing and leave TfidfVectorizer lowercase=True because it is harmless on already-lowercased text.
rationale: The paper says the text was converted to lowercase and does not say the vectorizer lowercasing was disabled.
quote: the text was converted to lowercase.

gap: The exact regular expressions for the initial RT marker, URLs, user mentions and hashtag characters are not given.
options: Use robust case-insensitive regexes for leading RT, URLs and @mentions
chosen: Remove a leading RT marker, replace case-insensitive URLs and @mentions with url and user, delete # characters while keeping following text, then normalise whitespace.
rationale: This follows the stated preprocessing operations without adding stemming, stop-word removal or custom tokenisation.
quote: URLs and user mentions were replaced with url and user; # characters were removed while retaining hashtag text

gap: The exact Macro-F1 implementation and zero-division policy are not stated.
chosen: Use sklearn.metrics.f1_score with average='macro', labels set to all 11 labels, and zero_division=0.
rationale: The paper uses scikit-learn and states that each of the 11 labels contributes equally.
quote: Macro-F1 was the primary measure because each of the 11 labels contributed equally

gap: Random seeds and determinism controls are not reported.
options: Run once with deterministic defaults and fixed random_state where supported
chosen: Run once with fixed random_state=42 for any stochastic component; LinearSVC and TF-IDF fitting are otherwise deterministic.
rationale: The paper reports single-run values and describes the preprocessing as deterministic.
quote: The same deterministic preprocessing function was applied to the Train, Development and Test text fields.

gap: The exact meaning of balanced class weighting is not spelled out beyond the scikit-learn setting name.
options: Manually weight classes to inverse frequency
Use no weighting in the final model
chosen: Use sklearn class_weight='balanced', which assigns weights inversely proportional to class frequencies.
rationale: The locked configuration explicitly uses balanced class weighting and scikit-learn.
quote: The selected and locked configuration was LinearSVC with word unigram–bigram TF-IDF, C=0.5 and balanced class weighting.

gap: Whether the final Test evaluation is repeated across seeds or reported as a single deterministic run is not stated.
options: Fit once on Train+Development and evaluate once on Test
Repeat with multiple seeds and report mean/std
chosen: Fit once on Train+Development and evaluate once on Test, matching the no-further-tuning protocol.
rationale: The paper reports a single locked Test result and no confidence interval or repeated-run spread.

Use keyword matching on post text
chosen: Use case-insensitive event-field matching: strict contains typhoon or hurricane, broad additionally contains cyclone; train the specialist on the broad set.
rationale: The paper defines strict and broad filters and says the broad definition was used for specialist training.
quote: The broad filter additionally matched cyclone, producing 21,944 records
